title: Constructible cohomology strata of Psi-good oriented nearby cycles
statement: Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring with $m\Lambda=0$ for an integer $m\geq1$ invertible on $S$, and let $L$ be a constructible sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{Et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf], viewed in degree zero. Assume $(f,L)$ is $\Psi$-good [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles]. For every integer $q\geq0$, set $G_q=\mathcal H^q(R\Psi_fL)$ on the vanishing topos $V_f$ of that definition. There exist finite partitions $X=\coprod_\alpha X_\alpha$ and $S=\coprod_\beta S_\beta$ into constructible locally closed subschemes [def-constructible-stratification] such that the restriction of $G_q$ to every oriented subtopos $P_{\alpha\beta}=(X_\alpha)_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{S_{\mathrm{Et}}}(S_\beta)_{\mathrm{Et}}$ is locally constant with finite $\Lambda$-module values. Here $P_{\alpha\beta}$ is the left oriented product of [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal] for the composites $X_\alpha\to X\to S$ and $S_\beta\to S$ of the immersions with $f$ and the identity, and restriction means inverse image along the morphism $P_{\alpha\beta}\to V_f$ which the universal property of that lemma attaches to the projections composed with the immersions $X_\alpha\to X$, $S_\beta\to S$ and to the $2$-morphism of $P_{\alpha\beta}$. Locally constant with finite $\Lambda$-module values means: the restriction becomes a constant sheaf with value a finite $\Lambda$-module on each member of some covering of that subtopos. The partitions may depend on $q$. No vanishing bound in $q$ is asserted.

source.place: Lu–Zheng, Duality and nearby cycles over general bases, Theorem 4.27(2) and the definition of constructibility immediately after it, printed pp. 36–37 of the v7 author PDF. Specialize to a Noetherian base (hence finitely many irreducible components), finite Lambda (hence Noetherian), and a constructible sheaf in degree zero. This is the conditional cohomological-constructibility assertion, not the modification assertion (1). The proof explicitly treats general Noetherian torsion coefficient rings, pp. 37. Local archival PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Fix $q\geq0$ and put $K=L[0]$. Its only nonzero cohomology is $\mathcal H^0(K)=L$, which is constructible by hypothesis. Hence $K$ is bounded constructible by [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. No truncation is needed: the input already has amplitude $[0,0]$.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 4.27(2), printed p. 37; in the degree-zero case the bounded truncation is L itself.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-psi-proper-surjective-constructibility] to $f,K,q$ with the given finite coefficient ring and invertible annihilator $m$. It gives a proper surjective $p:T\to S$ for which $F_T=\mathcal H^q(R\Psi_{f_T}(p_X^*L))$ is constructible on $V_{f_T}$. This is cohomology of nearby cycles for $f_T$; the lemma supplies no constructibility assertion for $v^*G_q$.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 4.27(2), last sentence applying Orgogozo Theorem 8.1 to the bounded input, printed p. 37.

proof.text: For this Cartesian square, [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles] constructs $v:V_{f_T}\to V_f$ and $\beta:v^*R\Psi_fL\to R\Psi_{f_T}(p_X^*L)$. Since $(f,L)$ is $\Psi$-good, $\beta$ is an isomorphism. The same definition states that $v^*$ is exact for constant $\Lambda$ coefficients, so it preserves kernels, images and quotients in a representative complex; therefore $v^*G_q=v^*\mathcal H^q(R\Psi_fL)\cong\mathcal H^q(v^*R\Psi_fL)\cong F_T$. Use the finite strata and trivializing coverings witnessing constructibility of $F_T$: composing their constant-sheaf isomorphisms with this isomorphism gives the identical witnesses for $v^*G_q$ in [def-trf-oriented-constructible-sheaf]. This is the point where $\Psi$-goodness is used.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 4.27(2), the Psi-good comparison before the truncation argument, printed p. 37.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-psi-constructibility-descent] with $F=G_q$ and the proper surjective map $p$ just obtained. Step 3 establishes precisely its hypothesis that the inverse image $v^*F$ is constructible on $V_{f_T}$. Thus $G_q$ is constructible on $V_f$.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 4.27(2), first sentence using Orgogozo Lemma 10.5, printed p. 37.

proof.text: Unfold [def-trf-oriented-constructible-sheaf] with $Y=S$ and $b=1_S$. Its finite constructible locally closed strata give the required partitions of $X$ and $S$. Its restriction maps are exactly the universal-property maps in the statement, and its trivializing coverings have constant finite $\Lambda$-module values. These are all the requested clauses. Since $q$ was fixed arbitrarily, the partitions may depend on $q$ and no uniform vanishing assertion is used or deduced.

source.place: Definition immediately following Theorem 4.27, printed p. 37, specialized to finite Lambda.
